blocks.lead: ZPUI unblocks Discord, YouTube and other resources with a single switch. The app does almost everything by itself: picks a working strategy for your ISP, watches availability and recovers after failures. This section is the short version — every tab is described in detail in the sections on the left.

steps: Launch ZPUI — the bypass engine already ships with the installer, nothing extra to download.
Right after the startup screen the smart selection window opens: the app tests strategies and picks a working one for your provider. Just wait — it takes a few minutes.
Turn the Zapret toggle on. The indicator turns green once the bypass is up.

blocks.h: How it all fits together — in a nutshell

list: Home — bypass status, resource availability and problems at a glance.
Zapret — the core module: strategies, domain lists, game mode.
Proxy — the Telegram bridge and a SOCKS5 proxy for your phone and other devices.
DNS — changing DNS servers: helps with YouTube and needed for sharing the bypass.
Monitor — speeds, ping and devices connected to your proxies.
Settings — theme, language, autostart, updates, power saving.

blocks.h: Setting up the bypass — basic scenario

steps: The lightning in the sidebar opens the selection window: “Smart select” (the default) tests the best strategies for your operator, “Game select” — for online games, “Full sweep” — every strategy one by one. The best one is applied automatically.
A strategy is saved for your operator: when you switch providers or networks, the app applies the strategy saved for that operator — or starts a background selection if there is none yet.
If a strategy stops working over time (ISPs change equipment) — run the selection again. AutoSwitch on the Zapret tab does this for you automatically.

blocks.text: Sites open but YouTube videos do not: your ISP spoofs video server addresses. Turn on the toggle on the DNS tab — one click fixes it.
Something not working? Check “Troubleshooting” — it also explains how to reach support.

blocks.lead: The main screen: the state of every service and the overall bypass quality at a glance. Everything on it is clickable and updates live.

Whether custom DNS is on and how many sources are active. Click opens the DNS tab.

The resource stops counting towards availability — handy if the site is down on its own.

blocks.lead: The core module. Zapret modifies network packets so that the ISP equipment lets traffic to blocked sites through. One toggle turns it on — the rest is automated.

blocks.text: The Zapret engine is an independent program. In service mode (Settings → ZAPRET) it keeps running even with the app closed and starts together with Windows. That is why “Close app” in the tray does not stop it — the full “Quit” with a confirmation does.

rows.v: Status dot, engine version and your ISP — the network is detected automatically.
Turns the bypass on and off. Starting is asynchronous: the spinner spins until the engine is up.
Environment check: conflicts, VPN, file integrity. Helps find the cause of problems.
If availability drops below the threshold, the app switches the strategy by itself. The gear next to it sets the threshold (50–80%).
More than twenty ready-made strategies are built in, plus one universal of our own — the app creates and updates it by itself.
Click to apply (Zapret must be on). You can switch strategies as often as you like.
Tier — the score from the latest checks: S — excellent, D — dead. Hover for availability, key resources, speed — and the “weakest link”: what the strategy lacked compared to a direct connection.
The strategy’s game score — how well it suits online games (ping, platforms).
Display filter: show only strong tiers, only tested ones, or all. The current strategy is always visible.
A quick-test menu: check one strategy — regular or game-style — and refresh its tier without a full sweep. Works even when the cards are locked.
Domains that Zapret processes by your rules. One domain per line.
Resources that should not count towards availability checks (for example, a site that is down on its own).
Updated automatically from the server, read-only.

Separate handling of game traffic: all, TCP only, UDP only, or off. If the current strategy is not a game one, the app offers game strategies or a forced override. Applies to the running engine immediately, no reinstall.
Process all traffic or only IPs from the list: loaded / none / any. Next to it — the address count and the list update date. Changes apply on the fly too.

blocks.text: Do not run a third-party Zapret alongside ZPUI — the conflict will kill your internet.
If the engine crashes, the app starts recovery by itself: a window with stages, and on failure — a restart and another try. Failure notifications are restrained: no more than once every 2 minutes.

blocks.lead: Two independent services: the Telegram bridge (MTProto) — fast Telegram on this computer and your phone, and SOCKS5 — bypass for any device in your home network.

rows.v: Starts the bridge. Next to it — the mtproto://host:port status and connection/traffic counters.
Opens Telegram and the proxy is added automatically — just tap Enable.
For your phone: scan the QR with the camera — Telegram adds the proxy without manual settings. The link can be copied.
Opens the bridge to other Wi-Fi devices (by default — this PC only). One click to enable.
The proxy key. “Refresh” generates a new one — old connections have to be added again.
Bridge port, Fake TLS domain (disguises traffic as regular HTTPS), Cloudflare fallback and CF worker domains.

Enter it in the Wi-Fi settings on your phone or TV: proxy → manual → this address and port. The button copies it.
1080 by default, changeable in the field. No username or password needed.

blocks.text: The phone and the computer must be on the same network (one router). If the phone will not connect, check whether Windows Firewall blocks the port.

blocks.lead: Replacing your computer’s DNS servers. DNS cannot beat DPI, but it fixes address spoofing (typical for YouTube) and is needed to share the bypass with other devices.

Green — the source’s servers respond, red — they do not (the toggle is locked). Dead sources are switched off automatically.
The source was temporarily turned off by the ZPUI server — for example, its provider is being blocked.

blocks.text: After you turn DNS off, your ISP’s settings (DHCP) come back automatically — nothing to fix by hand.

blocks.h: How to remove the Zapret engine

rows.v: Settings → the ZAPRET section → “Remove service”: the engine stops and no longer starts with the system. The files remain — “Full reinstall” brings it back.
Windows Settings → Apps → ZPUI → “Uninstall”. The uninstaller stops ZPUI and the engine by itself, removing the zapret service and its files; your data (settings, lists) can be kept with a checkbox.

blocks.lead: The most common problems and how to solve them — from simple to advanced.

blocks.text: Turn Zapret off — network settings come back automatically. If that did not help, reboot the computer.

steps: Make sure Zapret is on (green dot on the Zapret tab).
Run the selection: Auto-select in the sidebar → “Smart select”.
Open “Diagnostics” on the Zapret tab — it shows conflicts and environment problems.
Flush the DNS cache: Win+R → cmd → ipconfig /flushdns.

blocks.h: Sites open but YouTube videos do not

blocks.text: Your ISP spoofs video server addresses — Zapret cannot bypass that, a clean resolver is needed. Open the DNS tab: Xbox DNS or any other source will do.

blocks.h: The proxy does not work on my phone

list: The phone and the computer must be on the same Wi-Fi network (one router).
For SOCKS5, check whether the firewall blocks the port (1080 by default).
For Telegram, use the QR code — it enables LAN access by itself.
An error code like UPD-EXXX points to the stage: download, unpacking, integrity.
Copy the code and the error text into the support group — we will help.

blocks.text: Check logs\boot.log in the app folder (or %TEMP%\zpui-boot.log) — the startup error is described there. The in-app journal is the sheet icon in the sidebar.

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard way to give an AI agent (ZCode, Claude Desktop, etc.) access to the app. The agent can read status, switch strategies, run auto-select, control DNS and proxy, and read logs — you decide whether to allow it.

steps: Click the MCP button in the left sidebar and turn on the toggle in the “Server” section.
In the “Agent config” section press "Copy" — the ready-made JSON already contains the address, port and access key.
Paste the config into your agent's MCP settings (the MCP servers config file or the add-server dialog).
Done: the agent gets ZPUI tools, and connected agents are listed in the “Agents” section — name, address and last-seen time.

blocks.text: An agent gets real control over the app — connect only AI agents you trust. Dangerous actions (updates, uninstall, account, telemetry) are not exposed to agents.

blocks.lead: The app runs on a bypass engine: it subtly modifies network traffic so blocked sites open. Strategies, the service and auto-select work with it as before.

rows.v: The engine ships with the ZPUI installer — it is ready to work right after the app is installed. If files get corrupted, the app downloads and installs them again by itself.
The engine has its own update channel, separate from the app: Settings → ZAPRET → “Update”. Sources — the ZPUI server, a Yandex.Disk fallback and GitHub; the freshest version wins.
When updating from older versions, the app detects the previous engine generation by itself, removes it and installs the current one — your settings, lists and strategies are kept.

blocks.text: After the engine is installed or updated, the bypass restarts automatically — no action needed.

lua.intro1: A strategy is the bypass engine command line. Profiles are separated by the --new token: profile filters (--filter-tcp/--filter-udp, --filter-l7, --payload, --hostlist/--ipset) select the traffic, and --lua-desync=function:param=value functions decide what to do with it.
lua.intro2: Interception is global: --wf-tcp-out/--wf-udp-out for ports, --wf-raw-part for precise WinDivert filter files (windivert.filter folder). Fake packets are attached as blobs: --blob=name:@file; libraries load via --lua-init=@file.
lua.intro3: You can build your own strategy from any bundled one: right-click a strategy card and pick “Edit a copy” — the editor validates the syntax before saving.

fns.fake: Fake packets ahead of the real one: DPI inspects the fake, the server drops it. Params: blob, repeats, tcp_seq (seq overlap), tls_mod, ip_autottl, tcp_md5.
fns.multisplit: Splits the outgoing packet into segments at position pos; seqovl and seqovl_pattern add a fake-pattern overlap.
fns.fakedsplit: Split with a fake first part: DPI sees the fake, the server gets the real segments.
fns.multidisorder: Segments are sent out of order; only the server reassembles them correctly.
fns.fakeddisorder: Out-of-order segments plus a fake part.
fns.hostfakesplit: Split at the host marker (pos=host) with a fake sent ahead.
fns.wssize: Lowers the window scale for the whole connection so DPI cannot see the full picture; limit with --out-range.
fns.synack_split: Splits the first packet after the handshake.
fns.http_domcase: Mixed-case domain in the HTTP request.
fns.http_hostcase: Rewrites the case/value of the Host header.
fns.http_methodeol: Line break after the HTTP method — breaks signatures.
fns.http_unixeol: Replaces CRLF with LF in HTTP headers.
fns.tls_client_hello_clone: Clones the TLS ClientHello to fill the window.
fns.syndata: Data carried in the SYN packet.
fns.rst: Sends a TCP RST as the client.
fns.tcpseg: Manual TCP segmentation of arbitrary data.
fns.oob: Part of the data is sent as TCP Urgent (out-of-band).
fns.udplen: Increases the UDP packet length with padding.

lua.introShort: A strategy is bypass engine arguments: profiles via --new, functions via --lua-desync, blobs via --blob. This tab holds Lua scripts: yours in lua-user, engine libraries in lua. Functions defined in scripts can be called from any strategy.
